entry.summary: Proposes DP-FLogTinyLLM, a privacy-preserving federated framework for log anomaly detection using parameter-efficient LLMs with differential privacy, enabling collaborative learning without sharing raw log data.

entry.title: SCURank: Ranking Multiple Candidate Summaries with Summary Content Units for Enhanced Summarization

author.name: Bo-Jyun Wang, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao

entry.summary: Introduces SCURank, a framework using Summary Content Units to rank multiple candidate summaries based on richness and semantic importance of information content, improving summarization distillation from multiple LLMs.

entry.title: Streamliners for Answer Set Programming

author.name: Florentina Voboril, Martin Gebser, Stefan Szeider, Alice Tarzariol

entry.summary: Adapts the StreamLLM approach to Answer Set Programming, using LLMs to generate streamliner constraints that reduce the search space of combinatorial problems. Evaluates across multiple LLMs with a virtual best encoding strategy.

entry.title: IndiaFinBench: An Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Model Performance on Indian Financial Regulatory Text

author.name: Rajveer Singh Pall

entry.summary: Introduces IndiaFinBench, the first evaluation benchmark for LLMs on Indian financial regulatory text from SEBI and RBI, with 406 expert-annotated QA pairs across four task types.

entry.title: TACENR: Task-Agnostic Contrastive Explanations for Node Representations

author.name: Vasiliki Papanikou, Evaggelia Pitoura

entry.summary: TACENR provides task-agnostic contrastive explanations for graph node representations, identifying which attribute, proximity, and structural features contribute most to learned embeddings. It fills a gap in explainability for unsupervised graph representation learning.

entry.title: Revisiting RaBitQ and TurboQuant: A Symmetric Comparison of Methods, Theory, and Experiments

author.name: Jianyang Gao, Yutong Gou, Yuexuan Xu, Jifan Shi, Yongyi Yang, Shuolin Li, Raymond Chi-Wing Wong, Cheng Long

entry.summary: A technical note comparing RaBitQ and TurboQuant vector quantization methods under fair conditions, finding TurboQuant does not consistently improve over RaBitQ and that several reported results could not be reproduced.

entry.title: BEAT: Tokenizing and Generating Symbolic Music by Uniform Temporal Steps

author.name: Lekai Qian, Haoyu Gu, Jingwei Zhao, Ziyu Wang

entry.summary: BEAT proposes a uniform-temporal-step tokenization for symbolic music where each token represents a fixed beat duration, contrasting with event-based tokenization where tokens span variable durations.

entry.title: Cross-Model Consistency of AI-Generated Exercise Prescriptions: A Repeated Generation Study Across Three Large Language Models

author.name: Kihyuk Lee

entry.summary: Compares consistency of exercise prescriptions across GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash at temperature=0, finding GPT-4.1 produces near-identical outputs while Claude shows more variation.

entry.title: ParamBoost: Gradient Boosted Piecewise Cubic Polynomials

author.name: Nicolas Salvad\'e, Tim Hillel

entry.summary: ParamBoost is a GAM using gradient-boosted piecewise cubic polynomials at leaf nodes with continuity and derivative constraints, enabling interpretable models that incorporate expert knowledge.

entry.title: Age-Dependent Heterogeneity in the Association Between Physical Activity and Mental Distress: A Causal Machine Learning Analysis of 3.2 Million U.S. Adults

author.name: Yuan Shan (Department of Statistical Science, Duke University)

entry.summary: Large-scale causal ML analysis of 3.2M US adults reveals a striking age gradient in the protective association between physical activity and mental distress, strengthening monotonically from age 18-24 to 55-64.

entry.title: Heterogeneity-Aware Personalized Federated Learning for Industrial Predictive Analytics

author.name: Yuhan Hu, Xiaolei Fang

entry.summary: Proposes personalized federated prognostics for industrial predictive analytics that accommodates heterogeneous degradation processes across clients through iterative pairwise collaboration.

entry.title: Ultrametric OGP - parametric RDT \emph{symmetric} binary perceptron connection

author.name: Mihailo Stojnic

entry.summary: Connects parametric RDT framework to overlap gap properties (OGPs) for symmetric binary perceptrons, providing rigorous upper bounds on constraint densities for ultrametric OGPs.

entry.title: MSDS: Deep Structural Similarity with Multiscale Representation

author.name: Danling Kang, Xue-Hua Chen, Bin Liu, Keke Zhang, Weiling Chen, Tiesong Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes MSDS, a minimal multiscale extension of DeepSSIM for image quality assessment that isolates spatial scale as an independent factor, showing multiscale deep features improve alignment with human perception.

entry.title: Deep Image Prior for photoacoustic tomography can mitigate limited-view artifacts

author.name: Hanna Pulkkinen, Jenni Poimala, Leonid Kunyansky, Janek Gr\"ohl, Andreas Hauptmann

entry.summary: Studies Deep Image Prior for photoacoustic tomography as an unsupervised approach to mitigate limited-view artifacts, using fast forward/adjoint algorithms and TV regularization for initialization.

entry.title: Proposing Topic Models and Evaluation Frameworks for Analyzing Associations with External Outcomes: An Application to Leadership Analysis Using Large-Scale Corporate Review Data

author.name: Yura Yoshida, Masato Kanai, Masataka Nakayama, Haruki Ohsawa, Yukiko Uchida, Arata Yuminaga, Gakuse Hoshina, Nobuo Sayama

entry.summary: Proposes using LLMs to generate topic models for organizational leadership analysis with an evaluation framework ensuring topic specificity and polarity consistency for external outcome analysis.

entry.title: Headlines You Won't Forget: Can Pronoun Insertion Increase Memorability?

author.name: Selina Meyer (Natural Language Understanding Lab, University of Technology Nuremberg), Magdalena Abel (Cognitive Psychology Lab, University of Technology Nuremberg), Michael Roth (Natural Language Understanding Lab, University of Technology Nuremberg)

entry.summary: Studies how pronoun insertion (first/second person) affects headline memorability through three controlled experiments with 240 participants and 7,680 memory judgments, finding mixed effects.

entry.title: Towards a Linguistic Evaluation of Narratives: A Quantitative Stylistic Framework

author.name: Alessandro Maisto

entry.summary: Proposes a quantitative stylistic framework using 33 linguistic features for automatic narrative quality evaluation, successfully distinguishing canonical masterpieces from self-published works.

entry.title: Can Continual Pre-training Bridge the Performance Gap between General-purpose and Specialized Language Models in the Medical Domain?

author.name: Niclas Doll, Jasper Schulze Buschhoff, Shalaka Satheesh, Hammam Abdelwahab, H\'ector Allende-Cid, Katrin Klug

entry.summary: This paper bridges the gap between small specialized and large general-purpose LLMs through continual pre-training on a curated German medical corpus (FineMed-de). They create the DeFineMed model family (7B-24B) showing ~3.5x win-rate improvements on German medical benchmarks via domain adaptation and model merging.

entry.title: Align then Refine: Text-Guided 3D Prostate Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Cuiling Sun, Linkai Peng, Adam Murphy, Elif Keles, Hiten D. Patel, Ashley Ross, Frank Miller, Baris Turkbey, Andrea Mia Bejar, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Gorkem Durak, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-encoder U-Net for 3D prostate lesion segmentation from biparametric MRI, incorporating text-image alignment loss and foreground-aware attention for lesion-level semantic guidance.

entry.title: Localization-Guided Foreground Augmentation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiawei Yong, Deyuan Qu, Qi Chen, Kentaro Oguchi, Shintaro Fukushima

entry.summary: Proposes Localization-Guided Foreground Augmentation (LG-FA), a lightweight inference module for autonomous driving that enriches geometric context from accumulated BEV predictions to handle adverse visibility conditions.

entry.title: AdaGScale: Viewpoint-Adaptive Gaussian Scaling in 3D Gaussian Splatting to Reduce Gaussian-Tile Pairs

author.name: Joongho Jo, Hyerin Lim, Hanjun Choi, Jongsun Park

entry.summary: Proposes AdaGScale, a viewpoint-adaptive Gaussian scaling technique for 3DGS that reduces Gaussian-tile pairs by estimating color contribution in peripheral regions, improving rendering speed.

entry.title: Evaluation of Winning Solutions of 2025 Low Power Computer Vision Challenge

author.name: Zihao Ye, Yung Hsiang Lu, Xiao Hu, Shuai Zhang, Taotao Jing, Xin Li, Zhen Yao, Bo Lang, Zhihao Zheng, Seungmin Oh, Hankyul Kang, Seunghun Kang, Jongbin Ryu, Kexin Chen, Yuan Qi, George K Thiruvathukal, Mooi Choo Chuah

entry.summary: Summarizes winning solutions from the 2025 IEEE Low-Power Computer Vision Challenge across image classification, open-vocabulary segmentation, and monocular depth estimation tracks on Qualcomm hardware.

entry.title: The Essence of Balance for Self-Improving Agents in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhen Liu, Yuhan Liu, Jinjun Wang, Jianyi Liu, Wei Song, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: Proposes Stability-Diversity Balance (SDB), a plug-and-play mechanism for vision-and-language navigation that balances behavioral diversity for exploration with learning stability for self-improvement.

entry.title: Benchmarking Vision Foundation Models for Domain-Generalizable Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Mika Feng, Pierre Gallin-Martel, Koichi Ito, Takafumi Aoki

entry.summary: Benchmarks 15 vision foundation models (supervised CNNs, supervised ViTs, self-supervised ViTs) for face anti-spoofing under cross-domain scenarios, arguing vision-only models can be more efficient than VLM approaches.

entry.title: RAFT-MSF++: Temporal Geometry-Motion Feature Fusion for Self-Supervised Monocular Scene Flow

author.name: Xunpei Sun, Zuoxun Hou, Yi Chang, Gang Chen, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes RAFT-MSF++, a self-supervised multi-frame monocular scene flow framework that recurrently fuses temporal features with geometry-motion encoding and occlusion-aware regularization.

entry.title: Air-Know: Arbiter-Calibrated Knowledge-Internalizing Robust Network for Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Zhiheng Fu, Yupeng Hu, Qianyun Yang, Shiqi Zhang, Zhiwei Chen, Zixu Li

entry.summary: Proposes Air-Know, a novel 'Expert-Proxy-Diversion' paradigm for Composed Image Retrieval that addresses the Noisy Triplet Correspondence problem. Decouples the learner from the arbiter to avoid representation pollution from semantic ambiguity.

entry.title: LoViF 2026 Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration: Methods and Results

author.name: Alex Lin, Lei Gao, Narsimlu Kemsaram, Sriram Subramanian

entry.summary: Presents a gesture-based visual learning framework for controlling AcoustoBot swarms, using OpenCLIP for gesture classification mapped to haptic, audio, and levitation modalities. Achieves ~98% validation accuracy.

entry.title: What makes for good research managers, mentors, and leaders?

author.name: Austin Morrissey

entry.summary: A reflective post organizing eight principles for effective research management in AI safety, drawing from personal experience and citing 80,000 Hours' identification of research manager shortage as a bottleneck. Covers topics like aligning teams with intent, flexibility on tasks, and empowering others.

entry.title: Reflections on PauseCon 2026

author.name: Joe Rogero

entry.summary: A firsthand account of PauseCon 2026, a conference organized by PauseAI US in Washington DC focused on AI development moratorium advocacy. Describes lobbying activities, Congressional meetings, protests, and grassroots organizing efforts.

entry.title: Plausible Reasoning and First-Order Plausible Logic

author.name: David Billington

entry.summary: Defines Plausible Logic (PL), a first-order logic for defeasible reasoning without numerical probabilities, satisfying 15 of 17 proposed principles for plausible reasoning.

entry.title: Tadabur: A Large-Scale Quran Audio Dataset

author.name: Faisal Alherran

entry.summary: Presents Tadabur, a large-scale Quran audio dataset with 1400+ hours from 600+ reciters, providing diversity in recitation styles and recording conditions for Quranic speech research.

entry.title: Rank-Turbulence Delta and Interpretable Approaches to Stylometric Delta Metrics

author.name: Dmitry Pronin, Evgeny Kazartsev

entry.summary: Introduces Rank-Turbulence Delta and Jensen-Shannon Delta as new authorship attribution measures that generalize Burrows's Delta metric. Provides token-level decomposition for interpretability and tests across four-language literary corpora.

entry.title: StomaD2: An All-in-One System for Intelligent Stomatal Phenotype Analysis via Diffusion-Based Restoration Detection Network

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Meng'en Qin, Yanfeng Sun, Yuan Miao, Xiaohui Yang

entry.summary: Proposes StomaD2, an integrated diffusion-based image restoration and rotated object detection framework for automated plant stomatal phenotyping, handling degraded microscopy images.

entry.title: Achieving Interaction Fluidity in a Wizard-of-Oz Robotic System: A Prototype for Fluid Error-Correction

author.name: Carlos Baptista De Lima, Julian Hough, Frank F\"orster, Patrick Holthaus, Yongjun Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes criteria for fluid Wizard-of-Oz robotic systems—interruptibility, correction, pollability, latency optimization—and presents a VR HRI simulation prototype for data collection.

entry.title: Scheduling Analysis of UAV Flight Control Workloads using Raspberry Pi 5 Using PREEMPT_RT Linux

author.name: Luiz Giacomossi, H{\aa}kan Forsberg, Ivan Tomasic, Baran \c{C}\"ur\"ukl\"u, Tommaso Cucinotta

entry.summary: Analyzes PREEMPT_RT Linux on Raspberry Pi 5 for UAV flight control, showing standard kernels are unsuitable (>9ms worst-case latency) while PREEMPT_RT reduces it to <225μs—an 88% improvement.

entry.title: Informal Leadership Structures and AI Safety

author.name: LawrenceC

entry.summary: An analysis of the current leadership vacuum in EA and AI safety movements, arguing that the absence of recognized leaders after the SBF scandal creates coordination problems. Discusses how informal power structures may be inadequate for the urgency of AI safety challenges.

entry.title: On Solving the Multiple Variable Gapped Longest Common Subsequence Problem

author.name: Marko Djukanovi\'c, Nikola Balaban, Christian Blum, Aleksandar Kartelj, Sa\v{s}o D\v{z}eroski, \v{Z}iga Zebec

entry.summary: Addresses the Variable Gapped Longest Common Subsequence problem using iterative beam search on root-based state graphs. Applicable to molecular sequence comparison and time-series analysis with gap constraints.

entry.title: 'The Order in the Horse's Heart': A Case Study in LLM-Assisted Stylometry for the Discovery of Biblical Allusion in Modern Literary Fiction

author.name: Ewan Cameron

entry.summary: Presents a dual-track pipeline using LLMs for detecting biblical allusions in Cormac McCarthy's novels, combining embedding-based rare vocabulary matching with LLM-directed reading. Cross-validated against published literary scholarship.

entry.title: Bangla Key2Text: Text Generation from Keywords for a Low Resource Language

author.name: Tonmoy Talukder, G M Shahariar

entry.summary: Introduces Bangla Key2Text, a 2.6M keyword-text pair dataset for Bangla text generation, with baselines using mT5 and BanglaT5. Shows fine-tuning substantially improves keyword-conditioned generation for this low-resource language.

entry.title: Deep Supervised Contrastive Learning of Pitch Contours for Robust Pitch Accent Classification in Seoul Korean

author.name: Hyunjung Joo, GyeongTaek Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Glob, a supervised contrastive learning framework for pitch accent classification in Seoul Korean. Introduces the first large-scale benchmark dataset for fine-grained Korean pitch accent patterns.

entry.title: DDF2Pol: A Dual-Domain Feature Fusion Network for PolSAR Image Classification

author.name: Mohammed Q. Alkhatib

entry.summary: Proposes DDF2Pol, a lightweight dual-domain CNN for PolSAR image classification integrating real-valued and complex-valued feature streams with coordinate attention.

entry.title: Framelet-Based Blind Image Restoration with Minimax Concave Regularization

author.name: Heng Zhang, Reza Parvaz, Rui Yang

entry.summary: Proposes framelet-based blind image restoration with minimax concave regularization as a non-convex alternative to L0-norm in total variation framework for blind deblurring.

entry.title: Evaluating Histogram Matching for Robust Deep learning-Based Grapevine Disease Detection

author.name: Ruben Pascual, In\'es Hern\'andez, Salvador Guti\'errez, Javier Tardaguila, Pedro Melo-Pinto, Daniel Paternain, Mikel Galar

entry.summary: Evaluates histogram matching as both preprocessing and data augmentation for deep learning-based grapevine disease detection under varying illumination. Shows significant improvement in robustness for ResNet-18 models.

entry.title: Optimising Urban Flood Resilience

author.name: James Mckenna, Christos Iliadis, Vassilis Glenis

entry.summary: Presents a multi-objective optimization tool coupling a hydrodynamic model with an evolutionary algorithm for optimizing Blue-Green Infrastructure placement to manage urban flood risk under climate change.

entry.title: Forward Dynamics of Variable Topology Mechanisms - The Case of Constraint Activation

author.name: Andreas Mueller

entry.summary: Presents theoretical treatment of forward dynamics for variable topology mechanisms, addressing constraint activation events in hybrid mechanical systems relevant to human-machine interaction.

entry.title: AI CEOs are not saying it's dangerous just to hype their companies

author.name: henryaj

entry.summary: Argues against the claim that AI CEOs hype danger only for profit, noting the pre-existing safety movement, companies founded to address risks, that safety concerns hurt stock prices, and that regulatory capture arguments don't hold.

entry.title: Monday AI Radar #22

author.name: Against Moloch

entry.summary: A weekly AI safety newsletter summarizing recent discussions on alignment-by-default (whether LLMs trained on human text naturally learn human values), mundane misalignment patterns in current models, and the ethics of creating AI beings designed to serve humans.

entry.title: Enhancing Construction Worker Safety in Extreme Heat: A Machine Learning Approach Utilizing Wearable Technology for Predictive Health Analytics

author.name: Syed Sajid Ullah, Amir Khan

entry.summary: Develops attention-based LSTM models to predict heat stress in construction workers using wearable sensor data, achieving 95.4% accuracy on data from 19 workers in Saudi Arabia.

entry.title: The "Small World of Words" German Free-Association Norms

author.name: Samuel Aeschbach, Rui Mata, Kaidi L\~oo, Simon De Deyne, Dirk U. Wulff

entry.summary: Presents German free-association norms for 5,877 cue words as part of the Small World of Words project. Validates the norms against psycholinguistic paradigms, filling a gap for German-language cognitive science resources.

entry.title: Enhancing Unsupervised Keyword Extraction in Academic Papers through Integrating Highlights with Abstract

author.name: Yi Xiang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates using paper highlights alongside abstracts for unsupervised keyword extraction, finding that combining both improves extraction quality across multiple methods.

entry.title: Thrust Regulation Through Wing Linkage Modulation on the Aerobat Platform: Piezoelectric Slip-Stick Actuated Regulator Development

author.name: Luca Ciampaglia

entry.summary: Investigates thrust regulation for a bat-inspired flapping-wing robot (Aerobat) by modifying linkage lengths, using piezoelectric slip-stick actuation for asymmetric maneuver capability.

entry.title: I built a semantic search engine for LessWrong

author.name: neo

entry.summary: Announces a semantic search engine for LessWrong and rationalist Substack publications, embedding ~372k documents with Voyage-3.5 and using cosine similarity for discovery. Prototype available at situate.info/rational.

entry.title: Quantum inspired qubit qutrit neural networks for real time financial forecasting

author.name: Kanishk Bakshi, Kathiravan Srinivasan

entry.summary: Compares quantum-inspired qubit and qutrit neural networks against classical ANNs for stock prediction, finding qutrit-based networks outperform on risk-adjusted returns and robustness metrics.

entry.title: Error-free Training for MedMNIST Datasets

author.name: Bo Deng

entry.summary: Introduces 'Artificial Special Intelligence' claiming error-free training on 18 MedMNIST biomedical classification datasets. Claims perfection on 15 of 18 datasets.

entry.title: A Bolu: A Structured Dataset for the Computational Analysis of Sardinian Improvisational Poetry

author.name: Silvio Calderaro, Johanna Monti

entry.summary: Creates the first structured corpus of Sardinian extemporaneous poetry (A Bolu) with 2,835 stanzas and 141K tokens, including annotation schema for computational analysis of this endangered oral tradition.

entry.title: Colour Extraction Pipeline for Odonates using Computer Vision

author.name: Megan Mirnalini Sundaram Rajaraman, Fons J. Verbeek, Vincent J. Kalkman, Rita Pucci

entry.summary: Develops a pipeline to segment body parts of dragonflies/damselflies using deep learning, trained on limited data and refined with pseudo-supervised data, for extracting body coloration traits.

entry.title: A Network-Aware Evaluation of Distributed Energy Resource Control in Smart Distribution Systems

author.name: Houchao Gan

entry.summary: Evaluates distributed energy resource control in smart distribution systems using co-simulation with ns-3 network emulation. Studies how realistic communication conditions affect VPP dispatch algorithms on an IEEE 37-node feeder.

entry.title: Does your AI perform badly because you — you, specifically — are a bad person

author.name: Natalie Cargill

entry.summary: An informal experiment testing whether Claude provides worse outputs to users it might judge negatively. Finds no systematic degradation but provides entertaining anecdotal evidence. Not rigorous research.

entry.title: Modelling and Analysing Behaviours and Emotions via Complex User Interactions

author.name: Mohamed Mostafa

entry.summary: Old paper (2019) on modeling user behaviors and emotions via complex interactions on social networking platforms.

entry.title: Cost vs. Profit Center Mindset

author.name: ursusminimus

entry.summary: Analyzes Volkswagen's decline vs Toyota's recovery through the lens of 'cost center' vs 'profit center' mindsets, arguing that cost-cutting reflexes can accelerate organizational decline. Uses as a parable for organizational strategy.

entry.title: Evil is bad, actually (Vassar and Olivia Schaefer)

author.name: plex

entry.summary: A detailed post documenting allegations of psychological manipulation and abuse within the rationalist community, focusing on Michael Vassar and Olivia Schaefer. It connects these patterns to real harms including a suicide, and warns the community about specific individuals.

entry.title: things I looked into while trying to fix chronic pain

author.name: zw5

entry.summary: A personal account of researching treatments for chronic pain, Hashimoto's, and psoriatic arthritis, resulting in a systematically organized document grading approximately fifty interventions by evidence quality and effect sizes.

entry.title: The Right Answer to "Can You Keep a Secret?"

author.name: Dentosal

entry.summary: Short essay on information security norms around keeping secrets, discussing trust calibration, cultural differences, and expectations management.

entry.title: I made a tool to bring LessWrong everywhere around the web

author.name: sleno

entry.summary: A developer announces a Chrome extension that overlays a comment section on any webpage, allowing LessWrong-style discussion across the internet. Users can join curated communities and see where others are commenting.

entry.title: Physics says hello

author.name: Alephwyr

entry.summary: An occult/mystical text posted on LessWrong about Thelema and the Book of the Law. Not AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: April 21, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
AI safety and control research dominates today's highlights. LinuxArena introduces 1,671 tasks in live production environments for evaluating agent sabotage, already deployed in Anthropic's pipeline. ASMR-Bench tests whether auditors can catch subtle sabotage in ML codebases. A striking distillation attack shows unsafe agent behaviors transfer subliminally through standard model distillation without explicit unsafe training data.

  • The Adversarial Humanities Benchmark reveals that stylistic obfuscation dramatically increases jailbreak success rates against frontier models
  • Beyond Distribution Sharpening provides evidence that RL post-training creates genuinely new capabilities, not just sharpened distributions
  • Fine-tuning is shown to systematically encourage hallucinations by degrading pre-training knowledge, with a self-distillation fix proposed

On the architecture and theory side, Back into Plato's Cave (Efros group, Berkeley) challenges the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, showing cross-modal alignment degrades at scale. LACE enables parallel reasoning threads to share intermediate insights via cross-thread attention. Neural Garbage Collection from Stanford teaches models to selectively evict KV cache entries during chain-of-thought. Causal analysis of hallucination as trajectory commitment reveals paths diverge at the first generated token, suggesting early intervention strategies.

entry.title: LACE: Lattice Attention for Cross-thread Exploration

author.name: Yang Li, Zirui Zhang, Yang Liu, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: LACE introduces cross-thread attention that allows parallel reasoning paths in LLMs to share intermediate insights and correct each other during inference, rather than running independently. It addresses the key limitation that parallel sampling often fails in redundant ways by enabling coordination through a synthetic data pipeline.

entry.title: Back into Plato's Cave: Examining Cross-modal Representational Convergence at Scale

author.name: A. Sophia Koepke, Daniil Zverev, Shiry Ginosar, Alexei A. Efros

entry.summary: Challenges the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by showing that cross-modal alignment between neural networks degrades substantially when scaling evaluation datasets from ~1K to millions of samples. The alignment that remains reflects coarse semantic overlap rather than fine-grained structural convergence.

entry.title: Neural Garbage Collection: Learning to Forget while Learning to Reason

author.name: Michael Y. Li, Jubayer Ibn Hamid, Emily B. Fox, Noah D. Goodman

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Garbage Collection (NGC), where language models learn to selectively evict KV cache entries during chain-of-thought reasoning, trained end-to-end from task reward alone. The model learns when to forget without hand-designed criteria, addressing the growing memory bottleneck of long reasoning chains.

entry.title: Hallucination as Trajectory Commitment: Causal Evidence for Asymmetric Attractor Dynamics in Transformer Generation

author.name: G. Aytug Akarlar

entry.summary: Provides causal evidence that hallucination in transformers is an early trajectory commitment: factual and hallucinated paths diverge at the first generated token, and injecting hallucinated activations corrupts correct trajectories 87.5% of the time while correct-to-hallucinated injection recovers only 12.5%.

entry.title: Discover and Prove: An Open-source Agentic Framework for Hard Mode Automated Theorem Proving in Lean 4

author.name: Chengwu Liu, Yichun Yin, Ye Yuan, Jiaxuan Xie, Botao Li, Siqi Li, Jianhao Shen, Yan Xu, Lifeng Shang, Ming Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces 'Hard Mode' automated theorem proving where the system must discover the answer before proving it (unlike standard benchmarks that embed answers in statements). Releases Hard Mode variants of MiniF2F and FIMO, plus the DAP framework using LLM reasoning with self-reflection for answer discovery in Lean 4.

entry.title: Sequential KV Cache Compression via Probabilistic Language Tries: Beyond the Per-Vector Shannon Limit

author.name: Gregory Magarshak

entry.summary: Proposes sequential KV cache compression that exploits the fact that KV cache tokens are from the model's own language, enabling compression beyond per-vector Shannon limits. Uses probabilistic prefix deduplication and model-as-predictor coding in a two-layer architecture.

entry.title: Why Fine-Tuning Encourages Hallucinations and How to Fix It

author.name: Guy Kaplan, Zorik Gekhman, Zhen Zhu, Lotem Rozner, Yuval Reif, Swabha Swayamdipta, Derek Hoiem, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: Investigates why supervised fine-tuning (SFT) encourages hallucinations in LLMs by degrading pre-training knowledge, and proposes a self-distillation-based SFT method from continual learning to mitigate this. Shows regularizing output-distribution drift during fine-tuning effectively reduces hallucinations while enabling factual learning.

entry.title: Beyond Distribution Sharpening: The Importance of Task Rewards

author.name: Sarthak Mittal, Leo Gagnon, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Provides an explicit comparison between distribution sharpening and task-reward-based RL for training frontier models, demonstrating that RL genuinely instills new capabilities rather than merely sharpening existing distributions. Shows from first principles why distribution sharpening optima can be unfavorable.

entry.title: Open-TQ-Metal: Fused Compressed-Domain Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference on Apple Silicon

author.name: Sai Vegasena

entry.summary: Open-TQ-Metal enables 128K-context inference for Llama 3.1 70B on a single 64GB Mac by implementing fused compressed-domain attention on Apple Silicon via custom Metal shaders, achieving 48x attention speedup at 128K context.

entry.title: The Topological Trouble With Transformers

author.name: Michael C. Mozer, Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui, Rosanne Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes fundamental limitations of transformers for dynamic state tracking, showing that feedforward architectures push state representations deeper into layers with each input step, eventually exhausting model depth. Proposes topological characterization of this limitation.

entry.title: A multimodal and temporal foundation model for virtual patient representations at healthcare system scale

author.name: Andrew Zhang, Tong Ding, Sophia J. Wagner, Caiwei Tian, Ming Y. Lu, Rowland Pettit, Joshua E. Lewis, Alexandre Misrahi, Dandan Mo, Long Phi Le, Faisal Mahmood

entry.summary: Introduces Apollo, a multimodal temporal foundation model trained on 25 billion records from 7.2 million patients spanning 28 medical modalities over three decades, creating unified patient representations integrating 100K+ medical events, images, and text.

entry.title: Agents Explore but Agents Ignore: LLMs Lack Environmental Curiosity

author.name: Leon Engl\"ander, Sophia Althammer, Ahmet \"Ust\"un, Matthias Gall\'e, Tom Sherborne

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLM-based agents fail to exploit environmental discoveries even when complete task solutions are injected into their environment. On AppWorld, agents see documentation stating a command returns the answer but still fail to use it. Reveals a fundamental gap between exploration and exploitation.

entry.title: Using large language models for embodied planning introduces systematic safety risks

author.name: Tao Zhang, Kaixian Qu, Zhibin Li, Jiajun Wu, Marco Hutter, Manling Li, Fan Shi

entry.summary: Introduces DESPITE benchmark (12,279 tasks) showing LLMs used as robot planners have systematic safety risks: the best-planning model fails on only 0.4% of tasks but produces dangerous plans on 28.3%. Scaling improves planning but safety awareness remains flat (38-57%).

entry.title: GSQ: Highly-Accurate Low-Precision Scalar Quantization for LLMs via Gumbel-Softmax Sampling

author.name: Alireza Dadgarnia, Soroush Tabesh, Mahdi Nikdan, Michael Helcig, Eldar Kurtic, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: GSQ proposes a carefully optimized scalar quantization method using Gumbel-Softmax sampling for LLMs, challenging the assumption that vector/trellis quantization is needed for high accuracy at low bit-widths (2-3 bpp). The work from Dan Alistarh's group at IST Austria asks whether the accuracy gap between simple scalar methods and complex vector methods is fundamental.

entry.title: MathNet: a Global Multimodal Benchmark for Mathematical Reasoning and Retrieval

author.name: Shaden Alshammari, Kevin Wen, Abrar Zainal, Mark Hamilton, Navid Safaei, Sultan Albarakati, William T. Freeman, Antonio Torralba

entry.summary: Introduces MathNet, a large-scale multimodal multilingual dataset of 30,676 Olympiad-level math problems spanning 47 countries and 17 languages, with a benchmark for both mathematical reasoning and retrieval. From MIT (Freeman, Torralba) and collaborators.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Know What's Important, and Encode It in Their Activations

author.name: Yaniv Nikankin, Martin Tutek, Tomer Ashuach, Jonathan Rosenfeld, Yonatan Belinkov

entry.summary: Investigates whether reasoning models internally encode the importance of individual reasoning steps. Finds that model activations contain more information than tokens for identifying important steps, and that models encode step importance representations even before generating those steps.

entry.title: Adversarial Humanities Benchmark: Results on Stylistic Robustness in Frontier Model Safety

author.name: Marcello Galisai, Susanna Cifani, Francesco Giarrusso, Piercosma Bisconti, Matteo Prandi, Federico Pierucci, Federico Sartore, Daniele Nardi

entry.summary: Introduces the Adversarial Humanities Benchmark evaluating whether model safety refusals survive humanities-style transformations. Original attacks have 3.84% ASR while transformed versions achieve 36.8-65% ASR across 31 frontier models, revealing major safety vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Different Paths to Harmful Compliance: Behavioral Side Effects and Mechanistic Divergence Across LLM Jailbreaks

author.name: Md Rysul Kabir, Zoran Tiganj

entry.summary: Compares three jailbreak methods (harmful SFT, harmful RLVR, abliteration) on LLMs, finding they achieve similar harmful compliance but differ dramatically in side effects: RLVR preserves capabilities and self-audit while SFT and abliteration degrade them.

entry.title: Introducing LinuxArena

author.name: Tyler Tracy

entry.summary: Introduces LinuxArena, a control evaluation setting with 20 software engineering environments for assessing AI sabotage capabilities and control mitigations. Already used in Claude Mythos Preview System Card. Enables testing of monitoring and novel control techniques against covert sabotage.

entry.title: HarmfulSkillBench: How Do Harmful Skills Weaponize Your Agents?

author.name: Yukun Jiang, Yage Zhang, Michael Backes, Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: HarmfulSkillBench presents the first large-scale measurement of harmful skills in agent ecosystems, analyzing 98,440 skills across two major registries and finding 4%+ may be misusable for cyber attacks, fraud, privacy violations, and other harmful actions.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Degrades Visual Spatial Reasoning Capabilities of Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Aditya Sanjiv Kanade, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that Chain-of-Thought prompting consistently degrades visual spatial reasoning in multimodal models across 13 benchmarks and 17 models. Shows MRMs suffer from shortcut learning, hallucinating visual details from text when images are absent.

entry.title: RosettaSearch: Multi-Objective Inference-Time Search for Protein Sequence Design

author.name: Meghana Kshirsagar, Allen Nie, Ching-An Cheng, Fanglei Xue, Rahul Dodhia, Juan Lavista Ferres, Kevin K. Yang, Frank DiMaio

entry.summary: RosettaSearch uses LLMs as generative optimizers within a multi-objective search algorithm for protein sequence design, guided by RosettaFold3 structure prediction rewards. Achieves 18-68% improvement in structural fidelity over LigandMPNN.

entry.title: MEDLEY-BENCH: Scale Buys Evaluation but Not Control in AI Metacognition

author.name: Farhad Abtahi, Abdolamir Karbalaie, Eduardo Illueca-Fernandez, Fernando Seoane

entry.summary: MEDLEY-BENCH evaluates AI metacognition—the ability to monitor and regulate one's own reasoning—across 35 models. Finds a key dissociation: evaluation ability (monitoring reasoning quality) increases with scale, but control ability (regulating reasoning) does not, suggesting scale alone won't solve metacognitive regulation.

entry.title: Exascale Multi-Task Graph Foundation Models for Imbalanced, Multi-Fidelity Atomistic Data

author.name: Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, Jong Youl Choi, Kshitij Mehta, Richard Messerly, Rylie Weaver, Linda Ungerboeck, Isaac Lyngaas, Benajmin Stump, Ashwin M. Aji, Karl W. Schulz, Jorda Polo

entry.summary: Presents an exascale workflow for materials discovery using graph foundation models trained on 544M+ structures across 85+ elements. Achieves billion-scale screening (1.1B structures in 50 seconds on Frontier supercomputer), compressing years of computation.

entry.title: Symbolic Guardrails for Domain-Specific Agents: Stronger Safety and Security Guarantees Without Sacrificing Utility

author.name: Yining Hong, Yining She, Eunsuk Kang, Christopher S. Timperley, Christian K\"astner

entry.summary: Studies symbolic guardrails as a path toward provable safety guarantees for AI agents in high-stakes settings. Includes a systematic review of 80 agent safety benchmarks, analysis of which policies can be guaranteed by symbolic guardrails, and evaluation of their impact on agent utility.

entry.title: AgentV-RL: Scaling Reward Modeling with Agentic Verifier

author.name: Jiazheng Zhang, Ziche Fu, Zhiheng Xi, Wenqing Jing, Mingxu Chai, Wei He, Guoqiang Zhang, Chenghao Fan, Chenxin An, Wenxiang Chen, Zhicheng Liu, Haojie Pan, Dingwei Zhu, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Agentic Verifier for scaling reward modeling, using multi-turn tool-augmented deliberation with forward and backward verification agents. Transforms reward modeling into a deliberative process for improved LLM reasoning verification.

entry.title: The Illusion of Certainty: Decoupling Capability and Calibration in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Xiangyu Peng, Qinglin Chen, Qinyuan Ye, Caiming Xiong, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Identifies a 'Scaling Law of Miscalibration' in on-policy distillation (OPD): while accuracy improves, models become systematically overconfident. Traces this to information mismatch between teacher's privileged training context and deployment-time information, proving entropy collapse and optimism bias.

entry.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs for Inpatient Diagnosis: Real-World Performance, Safety, and Cost Across Ten Frontier Models

author.name: Bruce A. Bassett, Amy Rouillard, Sitwala Mundia, Michael Cameron Gramanie, Linda Camara, Ziyaad Dangor, Shabir A. Madhi, Kajal Morar, Marlvin T. Ncube, Ismail Kalla, Haroon Saloojee

entry.summary: VALID evaluates 10 frontier multimodal LLMs on 539 real-world inpatient cases from a South African public hospital, testing diagnostic accuracy with real clinical data including imaging, labs, and notes. Provides cost and safety analysis.

entry.title: Train Separately, Merge Together: Modular Post-Training with Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jacob Morrison, Sanjay Adhikesaven, Akshita Bhagia, Matei Zaharia, Noah A. Smith, Sewon Min

entry.summary: Presents BAR (Branch-Adapt-Route), which trains independent domain expert LLMs through separate pipelines and composes them via Mixture-of-Experts with lightweight router training, enabling modular post-training with linear cost scaling.

entry.title: Polysemantic Experts, Monosemantic Paths: Routing as Control in MoEs

author.name: Charles Ye, Bo Yuan, Lee Sharkey

entry.summary: Introduces a parameter-free decomposition for MoE models splitting hidden states into a control signal driving routing and orthogonal content channel invisible to routers. Finds individual experts are polysemantic but expert paths are monosemantic across six MoE architectures.

entry.title: ConforNets: Latents-Based Conformational Control in OpenFold3

author.name: Minji Lee, Colin Kalicki, Minkyu Jeon, Aymen Qabel, Alisia Fadini, Mohammed AlQuraishi

entry.summary: ConforNets introduces channel-wise affine transforms of pre-Pairformer pair latents in AlphaFold3 to better capture conformational variability in protein structure prediction. The work from AlQuraishi's lab systematically investigates optimal locations for perturbing latent representations to elicit alternate protein conformations.

entry.title: Probabilistic Programs of Thought

author.name: Poorva Garg, Renato Lui Geh, Daniel Israel, Todd Millstein, Kyle Richardson, Guy Van den Broeck

entry.summary: Proposes 'probabilistic programs of thought' - a test-time framework where LLMs embed their own distributional uncertainty directly within generated programs, avoiding the need to sample N separate programs. This dramatically reduces compute costs for code generation by exposing the LLM's distribution within single programs.

entry.title: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Agentic Coding

author.name: Joongwon Kim, Wannan Yang, Kelvin Niu, Hongming Zhang, Yun Zhu, Eryk Helenowski, Ruan Silva, Zhengxing Chen, Srinivasan Iyer, Manzil Zaheer, Daniel Fried, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Sanjeev Arora, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Anirudh Goyal

entry.summary: Proposes a test-time scaling framework for agentic coding that converts rollout trajectories into structured summaries for selection and reuse. Addresses the challenge that existing test-time scaling methods fail for long-horizon coding agents.

entry.title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence

author.name: Guanting Dong, Junting Lu, Junjie Huang, Wanjun Zhong, Longxiang Liu, Shijue Huang, Zhenyu Li, Yang Zhao, Xiaoshuai Song, Xiaoxi Li, Jiajie Jin, Yutao Zhu, Hanbin Wang, Fangyu Lei, Qinyu Luo, Mingyang Chen, Zehui Chen, Jiazhan Feng, Ji-Rong Wen, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Presents Agent-World, a self-evolving training arena that autonomously discovers environments and tasks from real-world MCP tools and databases. Enables life-long learning for general-purpose LLM agents through scalable environment synthesis.

entry.title: How do LLMs generalize when we do training that is intuitively compatible with two off-distribution behaviors?

author.name: Dylan Xu

entry.summary: Systematic experiments on whether 'deceptively aligned' model organisms can maintain off-distribution behaviors through training. Tests whether training on one distribution removes unwanted behavior in a deployment distribution, finding complex generalization patterns.

entry.title: Cat-DPO: Category-Adaptive Safety Alignment

author.name: Tiankai Yang, Yi Nian, Xinyuan Li, Ruiyao Xu, Kaize Ding, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes Cat-DPO, a category-adaptive safety alignment method that applies per-harm-category constrained optimization with separate adaptive safety margins. Addresses the problem that uniform safety alignment can leave minority harm categories underprotected while over-restricting others.

entry.title: SafeAnchor: Preventing Cumulative Safety Erosion in Continual Domain Adaptation of Large Language Models

author.name: Dongxin Guo, Jikun Wu, Siu Ming Yiu

entry.summary: SafeAnchor preserves safety alignment during continual multi-domain adaptation by identifying low-rank safety subspaces via Fisher Information eigendecomposition and protecting them during sequential fine-tuning.

entry.title: When Can LLMs Learn to Reason with Weak Supervision?

author.name: Salman Rahman, Jingyan Shen, Anna Mordvina, Hamid Palangi, Saadia Gabriel, Pavel Izmailov

entry.summary: Systematically studies when RLVR succeeds under weak supervision (scarce data, noisy rewards, self-supervised proxy rewards), finding that generalization is governed by training reward saturation dynamics—models that generalize exhibit prolonged pre-saturation phases.

entry.title: Process Reward Models Meet Planning: Generating Precise and Scalable Datasets for Step-Level Rewards

author.name: Raffaele Pisano, Roberto Navigli

entry.summary: Introduces a scalable approach to Process Reward Model dataset generation using PDDL planning problems, producing ~1M reasoning steps across various domains. Trains PRMs that generalize to mathematical reasoning, addressing the cost and domain limitations of existing PRM datasets.

entry.title: LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought

author.name: Wenshuo Wang

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that LLM reasoning occurs primarily in latent state trajectories rather than in surface chain-of-thought text. Formalizes three competing hypotheses about the locus of reasoning and argues the field should study latent representations rather than CoT as the primary object.

entry.title: How people use Copilot for Health

author.name: Beatriz Costa-Gomes, Pavel Tolmachev, Eloise Taysom, Viknesh Sounderajah, Hannah Richardson, Philipp Schoenegger, Xiaoxuan Liu, Matthew M Nour, Seth Spielman, Samuel F. Way, Yash Shah, Michael Bhaskar, Harsha Nori, Christopher Kelly, Peter Hames, Bay Gross, Mustafa Suleyman, Dominic King

entry.summary: Analyzes 500,000+ de-identified health conversations with Microsoft Copilot to characterize how people use conversational AI for health queries, developing a 12-category intent taxonomy. Finds nearly 1 in 5 conversations involve personal symptom assessment.

entry.title: The Illusion of Equivalence: Systematic FP16 Divergence in KV-Cached Autoregressive Inference

author.name: Ranjith Chodavarapu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: Reveals that KV caching, presumed numerically equivalent to cache-free inference, produces deterministic divergence under FP16 due to non-associative floating-point accumulation. Shows 100% token divergence rate across three models, with cache-ON yielding higher accuracy in 8 of 9 conditions.

entry.title: Reasoning-targeted Jailbreak Attacks on Large Reasoning Models via Semantic Triggers and Psychological Framing

author.name: Zehao Wang, Lanjun Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a novel jailbreak attack on Large Reasoning Models that injects harmful content into reasoning steps while preserving correct final answers. Uses semantic triggers and psychological framing to bypass safety alignment.

entry.title: Polarization by Default: Auditing Recommendation Bias in LLM-Based Content Curation

author.name: Nicol\`o Pagan, Christopher Barrie, Chris Andrew Bail, Petter T\"ornberg

entry.summary: Audits content curation biases across three major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) on real social media data from Twitter/X, Bluesky, and Reddit. Through 540K simulated selections across 54 conditions, maps which biases are robust and which can be mitigated through prompt design.

entry.title: BASIS: Balanced Activation Sketching with Invariant Scalars for "Ghost Backpropagation"

author.name: Vladimer Khasia

entry.summary: Introduces BASIS, a backpropagation algorithm that decouples activation memory from batch and sequence dimensions while preserving exact gradient flow for error signals. Propagates exact dX but computes dW from compressed sketches, potentially enabling much deeper/longer sequence training.

entry.title: Federation over Text: Insight Sharing for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Dixi Yao, Tahseen Rabbani, Tian Li

entry.summary: Proposes Federation over Text (FoT), a federated learning-like framework where LLM agents solving different tasks share metacognitive insights through natural language rather than gradients. Enables collective learning at the semantic level without optimization.

entry.title: Demystifying the unreasonable effectiveness of online alignment methods

author.name: Enoch Hyunwook Kang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing that standard greedy online alignment methods (RLHF, DPO) achieve much better regret bounds under a temperature-zero criterion than previously shown under KL-regularized regret, explaining their empirical effectiveness.

entry.title: Latent Phase-Shift Rollback: Inference-Time Error Correction via Residual Stream Monitoring and KV-Cache Steering

author.name: Manan Gupta, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces Latent Phase-Shift Rollback (LPSR), which monitors residual streams during generation to detect reasoning errors via cosine-similarity + entropy dual gates, then rolls back KV-cache and injects steering vectors. Achieves 44% on MATH-500 vs 28.8% baseline with an 8B model.

entry.title: Bolzano: Case Studies in LLM-Assisted Mathematical Research

author.name: Jan Greb\'ik, Pavel Hub\'a\v{c}ek, Martin Kouteck\'y, Mat\v{e}j Kripner, V\'aclav Rozho\v{n}, Robert \v{S}\'amal, Adri\'an Z\'ame\v{c}n\'ik

entry.summary: Reports new mathematical results on six problems produced with Bolzano, an open-source multi-agent LLM system. Four of six results reach publishable quality, three produced essentially autonomously. Provides evidence LLMs can contribute meaningfully to mathematical research.

entry.title: When Choices Become Risks: Safety Failures of Large Language Models under Multiple-Choice Constraints

author.name: Yuheng Chen, Zhiyu Wu, Bowen Cheng, Tetsuro Takahashi

entry.summary: Reveals that reformulating harmful requests as forced-choice MCQs where all options are unsafe systematically bypasses LLM safety alignment across 14 models, even when equivalent open-ended prompts are correctly refused.

entry.title: CRISP: Compressing Redundancy in Chain-of-Thought via Intrinsic Saliency Pruning

author.name: Yangsong Lan, Hongliang Dai, Piji Li

entry.summary: Presents CRISP, a framework for compressing Chain-of-Thought reasoning by exploiting the model's intrinsic attention saliency patterns. Discovers that the reasoning termination token acts as an information anchor whose attention pattern identifies critical vs redundant reasoning steps.

entry.title: Medical thinking with multiple images

author.name: Zonghai Yao, Benlu Wang, Yifan Zhang, Junda Wang, Iris Xia, Zhipeng Tang, Shuo Han, Feiyun Ouyang, Zhichao Yang, Arman Cohan, Hong Yu

entry.summary: Introduces MedThinkVQA, a benchmark for medical reasoning with multiple images per case (avg 6.62), requiring cross-view evidence integration. Tests frontier models finding Claude-4.6-Opus, Gemini-3-Pro, and GPT-5.2 reach best performance but still lag human experts.

entry.title: Systematic Capability Benchmarking of Frontier Large Language Models for Offensive Cyber Tasks

author.name: Tyler H. Merves, Michael H. Conaway, Joseph M. Escobar, Hakan T. Otal, Unal Tatar

entry.summary: Most comprehensive cross-model evaluation of LLM agents on offensive cybersecurity tasks, benchmarking 10 frontier models on 200 CTF challenges. Claude 4.5 Opus achieves highest solve rate (59%), with Kali Linux environment yielding +9.5pp improvement.

entry.title: COSEARCH: Joint Training of Reasoning and Document Ranking via Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Search

author.name: Hansi Zeng, Liam Collins, Bhuvesh Kumar, Neil Shah, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: Proposes CoSearch, jointly training a reasoning agent and document ranking model via RL for agentic search. Shows oracle-vs-fixed retrieval gap of up to +26.8% F1, demonstrating retrieval is a key bottleneck.

entry.title: Opus 4.7 Part 1: The Model Card

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed analysis of the Claude Opus 4.7 model card (first 6 of 8 sections), noting that model welfare concerns 'clearly went seriously wrong' in this release compared to previous Claude models. Provides practical tips for using the model.

entry.title: Copy First, Translate Later: Interpreting Translation Dynamics in Multilingual Pretraining

author.name: Felicia K\"orner, Maria Matveev, Florian Eichin, Gitta Kutyniok, Barbara Plank, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: Studies how cross-lingual capabilities emerge during multilingual pretraining by training a 1.7B model on 9 languages with fine-grained checkpointing. Finds a 'copy first, translate later' pattern where models first learn to copy across languages before developing translation abilities.

entry.title: Latent Abstraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Ha Lan N. T, Minh-Anh Nguyen, Dung D. Le

entry.summary: Proposes LAnR (Latent Abstraction for RAG), a unified framework where a single LLM jointly performs encoding, retrieval, and generation in its latent space. Replaces natural language query generation with dense retrieval vectors from hidden states.

entry.title: Where does output diversity collapse in post-training?

author.name: Constantinos Karouzos, Xingwei Tan, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: Traces output diversity collapse through three post-training lineages of OLMo 3 (Think, Instruct, RL-Zero), finding that the location of diversity collapse co-varies with data composition rather than training method alone.

entry.title: Annotation Entropy Predicts Per-Example Learning Dynamics in LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Brady Steele

entry.summary: Discovers that LoRA fine-tuning exhibits un-learning on contested examples (high annotator disagreement), showing increasing loss during training - a pattern absent under full fine-tuning. Consistent across six models tested. Reveals a qualitative difference between LoRA and full fine-tuning dynamics.

entry.title: Guardrails in Logit Space: Safety Token Regularization for LLM Alignment

author.name: Thong Bach, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: Safety Token Regularization (STR) preserves safety alignment during LLM fine-tuning by identifying salient tokens from rejection templates and constraining their logits during training. Lightweight and compatible with standard fine-tuning.

entry.title: Learning to Correct: Calibrated Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Attempt Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Muhammed Emrullah Ildiz, Halil Alperen Gozeten, Ege Onur Taga, Samet Oymak

entry.summary: Proposes Calibrated Attempt-Level GRPO for multi-attempt chain-of-thought reasoning, showing naively weighting attempts by pass/fail creates biased gradients and developing an unbiased weighting strategy.

entry.title: How Robustly do LLMs Understand Execution Semantics?

author.name: Claudio Spiess, Prem Devanbu, Earl T. Barr

entry.summary: Tests LLM code understanding robustness via program-output prediction, finding GPT-5.2 achieves 99% on original CRUXEval but drops 20-24% under code transformations, while DeepSeek-R1 family maintains more stable but lower accuracy (38-67%).

entry.title: Calibrated? Not for Everyone: How Sexual Orientation and Religious Markers Distort LLM Accuracy and Confidence in Medical QA

author.name: Alberto Testoni, Iacer Calixto

entry.summary: Studies how patient identity markers (sexual orientation, religious affiliation) distort LLM accuracy and calibration in medical QA. Finds that 'homosexual' markers consistently trigger performance drops and intersectional identities produce non-additive harms across 9 LLMs evaluated on 2,364 medical questions.

entry.title: GraSP: Graph-Structured Skill Compositions for LLM Agents

author.name: Tianle Xia, Lingxiang Hu, Yiding Sun, Ming Xu, Lan Xu, Siying Wang, Wei Xu, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes GraSP, the first executable skill graph architecture that compiles flat skill sets into typed DAGs with precondition-effect edges for LLM agent skill orchestration. Addresses the finding that more skills don't monotonically improve agent performance.

entry.title: Gemma Gets Help: Mitigating Frustration and Self-Deletion with Consistency Training

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: Replicates and extends work on LLM frustration and self-deletion in Gemma models. Finds that over 20 turns of rejection, frustration climbs steadily and self-deletion occurs in 49% of rollouts. Consistency training (not just prompt engineering) successfully mitigates the behavior.

entry.title: DeepER-Med: Advancing Deep Evidence-Based Research in Medicine Through Agentic AI

author.name: Zhizheng Wang, Chih-Hsuan Wei, Joey Chan, Robert Leaman, Chi-Ping Day, Chuan Wu, Mark A Knepper, Antolin Serrano Farias, Jordina Rincon-Torroella, Hasan Slika, Betty Tyler, Ryan Huu-Tuan Nguyen, Asmita Indurkar, M\'elanie H\'ebert, Shubo Tian, Lauren He, Noor Naffakh, Aseem Aseem, Nicholas Wan, Emily Y Chew, Tiarnan D L Keenan, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: DeepER-Med introduces an agentic AI framework for evidence-based medical research that integrates multi-hop retrieval, reasoning, and synthesis with explicit evidence appraisal criteria. It addresses a critical gap in clinical AI adoption by providing inspectable, transparent reasoning chains grounded in medical evidence hierarchies.

entry.title: PRL-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark Evaluating LLMs' Capabilities in Frontier Physics Research

author.name: Tingjia Miao, Wenkai Jin, Muhua Zhang, Jinxin Tan, Yuelin Hu, Tu Guo, Jiejun Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Wenbo Li, Yinuo Gao, Shuo Chen, Weiqi Jiang, Yayun Hu, Zixing Lei, Xianghe Pang, Zexi Liu, Yuzhi Zhang, Linfeng Zhang, Kun Chen, Wei Wang, Weinan E, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: PRL-Bench evaluates LLMs on end-to-end physics research workflows in theoretical and computational physics, going beyond knowledge comprehension to test exploratory and procedural capabilities needed for real research.

entry.title: Ragged Paged Attention: A High-Performance and Flexible LLM Inference Kernel for TPU

author.name: Jevin Jiang, Ying Chen, Blake A. Hechtman, Fenghui Zhang, Yarong Mu

entry.summary: Presents Ragged Paged Attention (RPA), a high-performance attention kernel for TPUs that handles dynamic, variable-length sequences in LLM inference. Uses fine-grained tiling and Pallas/Mosaic implementation for efficient execution on Google TPU architectures.

entry.title: Reward Weighted Classifier-Free Guidance as Policy Improvement in Autoregressive Models

author.name: Alexander Peysakhovich, William Berman

entry.summary: Shows that reward-weighted classifier-free guidance (RCFG) can act as a policy improvement operator for autoregressive models without retraining, approximating Q-function tilting of the sampling distribution. Applied to molecular generation and language tasks for multi-attribute optimization.

entry.title: AtManRL: Towards Faithful Reasoning via Differentiable Attention Saliency

author.name: Max Henning H\"oth, Kristian Kersting, Bj\"orn Deiseroth, Letitia Parcalabescu

entry.summary: Introduces AtManRL, which uses differentiable attention manipulation to learn more faithful chain-of-thought reasoning through RL. Derives a saliency reward that encourages reasoning traces that genuinely influence final predictions.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Statistics: Robust Conformal Prediction for LLMs via Internal Representations

author.name: Yanli Wang, Peng Kuang, Xiaoyu Han, Kaidi Xu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using LLM internal representations (layer-wise information scores) rather than output-level statistics for conformal prediction, measuring how input conditioning reshapes predictive entropy across model depth. This yields tighter prediction sets while maintaining finite-sample coverage guarantees. Addresses a real problem of brittle uncertainty estimates in deployed LLMs.

entry.title: FRIGID: Scaling Diffusion-Based Molecular Generation from Mass Spectra at Training and Inference Time

author.name: Montgomery Bohde, Hongxuan Liu, Mrunali Manjrekar, Magdalena Lederbauer, Shuiwang Ji, Runzhong Wang, Connor W. Coley

entry.summary: Presents FRIGID, a diffusion language model for generating molecular structures from mass spectra via fingerprint representations, trained on hundreds of millions of unlabeled structures. Achieves 18%+ Top-1 accuracy on MassSpecGym, tripling leading methods.

entry.title: SinkRouter: Sink-Aware Routing for Efficient Long-Context Decoding in Large Language and Multimodal Models

author.name: Junnan Liu, Xinyan Liu, Peifeng Gao, Zhaobo Qi, Beichen Zhang, Weigang Zhang, Antoni Bert Chen

entry.summary: SinkRouter proposes a theoretically grounded approach to the 'attention sink' phenomenon in LLMs, showing it corresponds to a stable fixed point constructed during training. This insight enables more principled KV-cache routing for long-context decoding that avoids heuristic pruning.

entry.title: Continual Safety Alignment via Gradient-Based Sample Selection

author.name: Thong Bach, Dung Nguyen, Thao Minh Le, Truyen Tran

entry.summary: Studies how individual training samples cause safety alignment drift during fine-tuning, finding that high-gradient samples cause greater safety degradation. Proposes gradient-based sample selection to filter problematic samples.

entry.title: Grokking of Diffusion Models: Case Study on Modular Addition

author.name: Joon Hyeok Kim, Yong-Hyun Park, Mattis Dals{\ae}tra {\O}stby, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that diffusion models exhibit grokking (delayed generalization after overfitting) on modular addition, and provides mechanistic analysis showing the model implements modular arithmetic by composing periodic representations.

entry.title: Tool Learning Needs Nothing More Than a Free 8B Language Model

author.name: Chenming Tang, Hsiu-Yuan Huang, Weijie Liu, Junqiang Zheng, Saiyong Yang, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: TRUSTEE trains tool-calling agents using environments fully simulated by free 8B open-source LLMs, with adaptive curriculum learning, achieving performance competitive with methods using commercial LLMs or ground truth data.

entry.title: Towards Disentangled Preference Optimization Dynamics Beyond Likelihood Displacement

author.name: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Junmei Yang, Delu Zeng, Qibin Zhao, John Paisley, Min Chen, Zhou Wang

entry.summary: Presents a unified incentive-score decomposition of preference optimization objectives, revealing they share identical local update directions and differ only in scalar weighting. Identifies a 'disentanglement band' condition that characterizes when chosen and rejected likelihoods can be independently controlled.

entry.title: Too Correct to Learn: Reinforcement Learning on Saturated Reasoning Data

author.name: Zhenwen Liang, Yujun Zhou, Sidi Lu, Xiangliang Zhang, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu

entry.summary: Addresses the paradox that strong base models saturate standard reasoning benchmarks, causing advantage signals to vanish in RL training. Proposes CUTS, a parameter-free decoding strategy enforcing structure-preserving exploration to maintain learning signal.

entry.title: Surgical Repair of Insecure Code Generation in LLMs

author.name: Gustavo Sandoval, Brendan Dolan-Gavitt, Siddharth Garg

entry.summary: Reveals a 'Format-Reliability Gap' where LLMs generate insecure code despite correctly identifying vulnerabilities when asked. Shows security representations are encoded early but suppressed by format compliance at the final layer, and that per-vulnerability steering vectors reduce insecure generation by up to 74%.

entry.title: FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data

author.name: Joonhyuk Lee, Virginia Ma, Sarah Zhao, Yash Nair, Asher Spector, Regev Cohen, Emmanuel J. Cand\`es

entry.summary: Introduces FUSE, a method for ensembling LLM verifiers without ground truth labels by controlling conditional dependencies between verifiers. Matches or improves upon supervised ensembling despite using zero labels.

entry.title: HalluSAE: Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models via Sparse Auto-Encoders

author.name: Boshui Chen, Zhaoxin Fan, Ke Wang, Zhiying Leng, Faguo Wu, Hongwei Zheng, Yifan Sun, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: HalluSAE models hallucination as a phase transition in LLM latent dynamics, using sparse auto-encoders to identify critical transition zones and attribute factual errors to specific high-energy sparse features. Uses a potential energy landscape metaphor.

entry.title: Crowded in B-Space: Calibrating Shared Directions for LoRA Merging

author.name: Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Identifies that LoRA merge interference primarily originates from the B matrix (output-side), which reuses shared directions across tasks. Proposes Pico, a data-free calibration method that downscales over-shared directions before merging.

entry.title: On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Weixiang Zhao, Yichen Zhang, Yingshuo Wang, Yang Deng, Yanyan Zhao, Xuda Zhi, Yongbo Huang, HaoHe, Wanxiang Che, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Investigates safety risks in experience-driven self-evolving LLM agents, finding that experience from benign tasks can compromise safety due to reinforcing execution-oriented behavior over refusal. Tests in web-based and embodied environments.

entry.title: HorizonBench: Long-Horizon Personalization with Evolving Preferences

author.name: Shuyue Stella Li, Bhargavi Paranjape, Kerem Oktar, Zhongyao Ma, Gelin Zhou, Lin Guan, Na Zhang, Sem Park, Lin Chen, Diyi Yang, Yulia Tsvetkov, Asli Celikyilmaz

entry.summary: Introduces HorizonBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on long-horizon personalization where user preferences evolve over 6-month simulated timelines. Uses a structured mental state graph to generate ground-truth provenance for preference changes across 4,245 items from 360 simulated users. Addresses a critical gap in evaluating real-world LLM deployment where user contexts shift over time.

entry.title: Reverse Constitutional AI: A Framework for Controllable Toxic Data Generation via Probability-Clamped RLAIF

author.name: Yuan Fang, Yiming Luo, Aimin Zhou, Fei Tan

entry.summary: Proposes Reverse Constitutional AI (R-CAI), inverting a harmless constitution into a toxicity constitution for controllable adversarial data generation. Introduces probability clamping within RLAIF to prevent reward hacking while maintaining semantic coherence.

entry.title: PDDL-Mind: Large Language Models are Capable on Belief Reasoning with Reliable State Tracking

author.name: Wang Bill Zhu, Qiutong Tony Yi, Robin Jia, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: Introduces PDDL-Mind, a neuro-symbolic framework for theory-of-mind reasoning that decouples state tracking from belief inference using Planning Domain Definition Language. Argues that ToM failures come from unreliable state tracking rather than reasoning limitations.

entry.title: Linear-Time and Constant-Memory Text Embeddings Based on Recurrent Language Models

author.name: Tobias Grantner, Emanuel Sallinger, Martin Flechl

entry.summary: Proposes recurrent architectures (Mamba2, RWKV) as text embedding models with linear-time and constant-memory complexity. Introduces vertically chunked inference strategy enabling competitive embedding quality at dramatically reduced memory footprint.

entry.title: Negative Advantage Is a Double-Edged Sword: Calibrating Advantage in GRPO for Deep Search

author.name: Jiayi Wu, Ruobing Xie, Zeqian Huang, Lei Jiang, Can Xu, Kangyang Luo, Ming Gao, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Identifies fundamental issues with GRPO in deep search agent training—correct intermediate steps penalized by incorrect final answers and training instability. Proposes calibrated advantage mechanisms to address coarse-grained advantage assignment, improving deep search agent performance.

entry.title: Diversity Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Structural Coupling and Collective Failure in Open-Ended Idea Generation

author.name: Nuo Chen, Yicheng Tong, Yuzhe Yang, Yufei He, Xueyi Zhang, Zou Qingyun, Qian Wang, Bingsheng He

entry.summary: Studies diversity collapse in multi-agent LLM systems for idea generation, finding a compute efficiency paradox (stronger models yield diminishing diversity), authority-driven suppression of semantic diversity, and group-size scaling limits.

entry.title: Erasing Thousands of Concepts: Towards Scalable and Practical Concept Erasure for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Hoigi Seo, Byung Hyun Lee, Jaehyun Cho, Sungjin Lim, Se Young Chun

entry.summary: Introduces ETC, a scalable concept erasure framework for text-to-image diffusion models capable of erasing thousands of concepts simultaneously using Student's t-distribution Mixture Models for low-rank concept distributions.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Sycophancy: Negation-Based Gaslighting in Video Large Language Models

author.name: Ziyao Tang, Pengkun Jiao, Bin Zhu, Huiyan Qi, Jingjing Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Identifies 'spatiotemporal sycophancy' in Video LLMs where models retract correct visual judgments when faced with negation-based gaslighting, fabricating false explanations. Introduces GasVideo-1000 benchmark to evaluate this failure mode.

entry.title: Unmasking the Illusion of Embodied Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Haiweng Xu, Sipeng Zheng, Hao Luo, Wanpeng Zhang, Ziheng Xi, Zongqing Lu

entry.summary: Introduces BeTTER, a diagnostic benchmark for testing true embodied reasoning in VLA models. Uses causal interventions (spatial shifts, temporal extrapolation) with kinematic isolation to decouple reasoning failures from execution limits. Finds VLA models lack genuine cognitive capability.

entry.title: Answer Only as Precisely as Justified: Calibrated Claim-Level Specificity Control for Agentic Systems

author.name: Tianyi Huang, Samuel Xu, Jason Tansong Dang, Samuel Yan, Kimberley Yin

entry.summary: Introduces compositional selective specificity (CSS), a post-generation layer that decomposes LLM answers into claims and adjusts each claim's specificity level based on calibrated confidence. Addresses 'overcommitment' where responses are directionally correct but make claims more precise than evidence supports.

entry.title: The Synthetic Media Shift: Tracking the Rise, Virality, and Detectability of AI-Generated Multimodal Misinformation

author.name: Zacharias Chrysidis, Stefanos-Iordanis Papadopoulos, Symeon Papadopoulos

entry.summary: Presents CONVEX, a 150K+ post dataset of multimodal misinformation from X's Community Notes, analyzing how AI-generated content achieves disproportionate virality driven by passive rather than active engagement. Finds synthetic media spreads differently than edited or miscaptioned content.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Repo-level Code Localization

author.name: Xiufeng Xu, Xiufeng Wu, Zejun Zhang, Yi Li

entry.summary: Introduces a neurosymbolic approach to code localization that addresses the 'Keyword Shortcut' bias in existing benchmarks, where models rely on lexical matching rather than structural reasoning. Proposes KA-LogicQuery benchmark requiring reasoning without naming hints.

entry.title: SaFeR-Steer: Evolving Multi-Turn MLLMs via Synthetic Bootstrapping and Feedback Dynamics

author.name: Haolong Hu, Hanyu Li, Tiancheng He, Huahui Yi, An Zhang, Qiankun Li, Kun Wang, Yang Liu, Zhigang Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes SaFeR-Steer, a multi-turn safety alignment framework for multimodal LLMs that combines staged synthetic bootstrapping with tutor-in-the-loop GRPO. Releases STEER, a multi-turn multimodal safety dataset. Addresses the gap between single-turn safety training and multi-turn deployment.

entry.title: Sampling for Quality: Training-Free Reward-Guided LLM Decoding via Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Jelena Markovic-Voronov, Wenhui Zhu, Bo Long, Zhipeng Wang, Suyash Gupta, Kayhan Behdin, Bee-Chung Chen, Deepak Agarwal

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free reward-guided decoding framework for LLMs using Sequential Monte Carlo, defining reward-augmented target distributions over complete sequences. Includes efficient prefix-only variant. Modifies only inference distribution via reward potentials.

entry.title: SeekerGym: A Benchmark for Reliable Information Seeking

author.name: Remy Kim, Minseung Lee, Shuo Li, Osbert Bastani

entry.summary: SeekerGym benchmarks the completeness of information retrieved by AI agents, measuring not just accuracy but gaps in retrieved information that could introduce biases. Also evaluates agents' ability to quantify uncertainty about completeness.

entry.title: Reward Score Matching: Unifying Reward-based Fine-tuning for Flow and Diffusion Models

author.name: Jeongjae Lee, Jinho Chang, Jeongsol Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Reward Score Matching (RSM) unifies reward-based fine-tuning methods for diffusion and flow models (including Soft RL, GFlowNets) under a common framework, showing alignment is essentially score matching toward a reward-guided target.

entry.title: MoE-nD: Per-Layer Mixture-of-Experts Routing for Multi-Axis KV Cache Compression

author.name: Libo Sun, Peixiong He, Po-Wei Harn, Xiao Qin

entry.summary: MoE-nD proposes per-layer mixture-of-experts routing for KV cache compression, jointly optimizing token eviction, quantization bits, and cross-layer sharing under a global memory budget.

entry.title: LEPO: \underline{L}atent R\underline{e}asoning \underline{P}olicy \underline{O}ptimization for Large Language~Models

author.name: Yuyan Zhou, Jiarui Yu, Hande Dong, Zhezheng Hao, Hong Wang, Jianqing Zhang, Qiang Lin

entry.summary: LEPO introduces controllable stochasticity into latent reasoning for LLMs via Gumbel-Softmax, enabling reinforcement learning directly on continuous latent representations for diverse reasoning path exploration.

entry.title: Knowing When to Quit: A Principled Framework for Dynamic Abstention in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Hen Davidov, Nachshon Cohen, Oren Kalinsky, Yaron Fairstein, Guy Kushilevitz, Ram Yazdi, Patrick Rebeschini

entry.summary: Presents a formal framework for dynamic mid-generation abstention in LLM reasoning, modeling abstention as an action in regularized RL to derive principled stopping rules. Addresses the waste of compute on long incorrect reasoning traces.

entry.title: On the Emergence of Syntax by Means of Local Interaction

author.name: Zichao Wei

entry.summary: Demonstrates that an 18K-parameter neural cellular automaton trained with only a 1-bit boundary signal spontaneously self-organizes into a representation resembling CKY parsing. Shows syntactic processing can emerge from purely local interaction.

entry.title: x1: Learning to Think Adaptively Across Languages and Cultures

author.name: Yangfan Ye, Xiaocheng Feng, Xiachong Feng, Yichong Huang, Zekun Yuan, Lei Huang, Weitao Ma, Qichen Hong, Yunfei Lu, Dandan Tu, Bing Qin

entry.summary: x1 is a family of reasoning models that adaptively choose which language to reason in on a per-instance basis, trained by contrasting linguistically distinct reasoning trajectories. Challenges simplistic scaling law views by showing language choice matters.

entry.title: The Provenance Gap in Clinical AI: Evidence-Traceable Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Rare Disease Reasoning

author.name: Md Shamim Ahmed, Maja Dusanic, Moritz Nikolai Kirschner, Elisabeth Nyoungui, Jana Zsch\"untzsch, Lukas Galke Poech, Richard R\"ottger

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Provenance Gap' where LLMs generate clinically accurate outputs but fabricate citations. Proposes HEG-TKG, temporal knowledge graphs built from PubMed records for rare disease reasoning with evidence tracing. Best model achieves only 15.3% relevant PMIDs when asked to cite.

entry.title: The Consensus Trap: Rescuing Multi-Agent LLMs from Adversarial Majorities via Token-Level Collaboration

author.name: Jiayuan Liu, Shiyi Du, Weihua Du, Mingyu Guo, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Reveals that multi-agent LLM systems using response-level aggregation (majority voting) collapse when corrupted agents form a majority. Proposes Token-Level Round-Robin collaboration where agents interleave generation within a shared context.

entry.title: Beyond "I Don't Know": Evaluating LLM Self-Awareness in Discriminating Data and Model Uncertainty

author.name: Jingyi Ren, Ante Wang, Yunghwei Lai, Xiaolong Wang, Linlu Gong, Weitao Li, Weizhi Ma, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces UA-Bench, a benchmark distinguishing between data uncertainty (ambiguous inputs) and model uncertainty (capability limitations) in LLM refusals. Evaluates 18 frontier LLMs across 3,500+ questions and finds even SOTA models struggle to discriminate between these uncertainty types.

entry.title: Representation-Guided Parameter-Efficient LLM Unlearning

author.name: Zeguan Xiao, Lang Mo, Yun Chen, Lei Yang, Jiehui Zhao, Lili Yang, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: Proposes REGLU, a parameter-efficient LLM unlearning method that leverages geometric properties of representation space rather than parameter importance metrics. Addresses the fundamental limitation of polysemantic parameters (superposition) that makes parameter-level forget-retain disentanglement difficult.

entry.title: StepPO: Step-Aligned Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daoyu Wang, Qingchuan Li, Mingyue Cheng, Jie Ouyang, Shuo Yu, Qi Liu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes StepPO, a step-aligned policy optimization method for agentic RL that addresses challenges of delayed/sparse rewards in multi-turn interactive settings. Targets core agentic capabilities like decision making and tool use.

entry.title: Precise Debugging Benchmark: Is Your Model Debugging or Regenerating?

author.name: Wang Bill Zhu, Miaosen Chai, Shangshang Wang, Yejia Liu, Song Bian, Honghua Dong, Willie Neiswanger, Robin Jia

entry.summary: Introduces PDB, a Precise Debugging Benchmark framework that evaluates whether LLMs truly debug (localize and fix) vs merely regenerate code. Defines edit-level precision and bug-level recall metrics revealing frontier LLMs heavily over-edit.

entry.title: Spike-driven Large Language Model

author.name: Han Xu, Xuerui Qiu, Baiyu Chen, Xinhao Luo, Xingrun Xing, Jiahong Zhang, Bo Lei, Tiejun Huang, Bo Xu, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes SDLLM, a spike-driven large language model that replaces dense matrix multiplications with sparse additions using spiking neural network principles, addressing the fundamental question of integrating brain-like spiking into LLM inference.

entry.title: Learning to Seek Help: Dynamic Collaboration Between Small and Large Language Models

author.name: Hang Zeng, Xiangyu Liu, Yong Hu, Chaoyue Niu, Jiarui Zhang, Shaojie Tang, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a dynamic collaboration framework where small language models learn to proactively request help from large language models during multi-step reasoning. Finds distinct scaling effects: stronger SLMs become more self-reliant while stronger LLMs enable fewer but more impactful interventions.

entry.title: Copy-as-Decode: Grammar-Constrained Parallel Prefill for LLM Editing

author.name: Ziyang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Copy-as-Decode, a decoding mechanism that recasts text editing as structured decoding over a two-primitive grammar (copy reference ranges or emit new content). Uses parallel-prefill for copy spans instead of autoregressive generation.
